glossary.Atlas: The product name users see. Windows desktop app (Atlas.exe) for authorized service technicians.
glossary.Almanac: Old/code name. Folders, DLLs and classes still say Almanac. Atlas = Almanac.
glossary.eAtlas: Atlas Web. Browser app for service managers + the Dashboard embedded inside desktop Atlas.
glossary.Service case: The record of one repair visit for one instrument. Everything the tech does is saved against it.
glossary.MTP: External system Atlas calls to get sales + warranty info for a serial number.
glossary.TWoD: Trimble's Salesforce org. Master source of products, companies, users, bulletins, authorizations.
glossary.DWCR: Dealer warranty claim submitted to Salesforce through OData by EXTERNAL technicians; MTP supplies eligibility data. Completes the case on success.
glossary.Service-Support: A Salesforce Case that INTERNAL technicians raise to ask for repair help.
glossary.OData Service: Primary backend of the desktop app (ASP.NET Web API on IIS, route /odata).
glossary.MongoDB (local): Windows service installed with Atlas. Local copy of server data so work is fast and possible offline.
glossary.Force Sync: Copies server data into local MongoDB (and pushes local changes up) in a fixed order.
glossary.EMS: Entitlement system for Atlas APPLICATION seats (not instrument licenses).
glossary.OKWS: Instrument license server asked for temporary instrument service keys.
glossary.BCS: Baseline Calibration Software – calibrates X/SX instruments; launched from Atlas Settings.
glossary.Detector: Plugin that auto-detects a connected instrument.
glossary.Service operation: Plugin (DLL/EXE) that does a repair/calibration step on the device and reports pass/fail.
glossary.Almanac API: The contract that detector/operation plugins implement (Trimble.Almanac.API).
glossary.Task list: Right-hand list in a service case: operations, parts, bulletins the tech will perform.
glossary.Collimator license: Restricted external license: baseline/collimator work, cannot create service cases or DWCR.
glossary.Environment Switch: INTERNAL tool to point a local install at prod/stage/dev. Never for field techs.
glossary.Reset Almanac Offline: Companion app that wipes local MongoDB so the next login rebuilds it.
glossary.Agentic AI: Trimble's AI chat used as the Repair Assistant; knowledge comes from manuals + bulletins.
glossary.Global Service: Thin HTTP API for OTHER Trimble teams (calibration PDF, recent closed cases...).

lessons.title: What is ATLAS?
lessons.hook: Imagine a pit-crew toolbox for surveying instruments. Atlas tells a technician what to fix, runs the tests, records the work and files the warranty claim.
goals: Explain the purpose of ATLAS and who uses it
Distinguish the Atlas product name from Almanac naming in code

items.d: Authorized service technicians at Trimble service centers and partners.
Guided repair: identify unit → open case → run operations → report/claim.
Windows desktop app: Atlas.exe (WPF, .NET Framework 4.8.1).
Atlas = Almanac. Search the code for 'Almanac'!

chapters: Atlas overview: purpose, users and the technician workflow

points: **Atlas** is an online **Service Repair Workflow** for **Authorized Service Technicians** of Trimble products.
One-stop shop: repair guidance, service software (detectors/operations), warranty claims, **service cases**, service history.
**Windows only** – it loads instrument plugins as DLLs/EXEs. That is why it is not a web app.
**Almanac** is the old name. Users see Atlas, the code still says Almanac (`AlmanacApp/Almanac`, `Trimble.Almanac.API`).

quiz.q: A teammate says 'the Almanac project'. What are they talking about?
o: Atlas – Almanac is the code/old name
quiz.why: Source, assemblies and install paths still say Almanac; the shipped product is Atlas.

lessons.title: The daily schedule
lessons.hook: Background jobs run in order; later ones wait for earlier ones.
goals: Identify the upstream owner of catalog and organization data
Trace incremental master-data distribution to Atlas clients
Explain the dependency on TWoD bulletin ingest
Describe recipient filtering and duplicate-mail tracking

items.d: Salesforce → Atlas SQL: companies, users, catalog, BOMs, bulletins, authorizations, sites.
Emails NEW bulletins to subscribed, authorized users (not everyone!).
Bulletins → Agentic KB. Manuals sync on upload instead.
Technician PC copies the fresh catalog into MongoDB.

points: **TWoD Master Data Sync** (Azure WebJob) runs daily **05:00**, incremental by `LastSyncTime` watermark.
**Atlas AI Sync** timer runs **06:00 UTC** – only after TWoD wrote `ServiceBulletin` for the day.
Bulletin **emails** also depend on TWoD ingest, then recipient filtering and duplicate tracking.
Atlas desktop later pulls the catalog with **Force Sync**.

quiz.q: Why does AI Sync run AFTER TWoD sync?
o: Bulletins must be in SQL for that day first
quiz.why: Bulletin ingest waits for the TWoD ServiceBulletin write.

lessons.title: Capstone: investigate with evidence
lessons.hook: Pick a symptom. Trace it through the documents. Say clearly what is proven, what is a guess, and what is missing.
goals: Connect the product journey to documented service and data boundaries
Distinguish supported explanations from hypotheses and missing evidence

items.d: A blocked step or a 'how does this work' question.
Read the project doc and the Functionality doc for that area.
Local MongoDB, OData, eAtlas/shared SQL, or OData-to-Salesforce for DWCR (MTP supplies eligibility data).
Quote the document section. Note any inspected code symbol.
Fact, hypothesis and the one missing piece of evidence.

points: Follow one repair across **desktop**, **local MongoDB**, the shared **SQL database** and the services around it.
A **network loss** or a **BCS Level 3** alert explains a documented restriction. It does not prove the cause of a real failure.
Always write three lists: **supported explanation**, **hypothesis**, **missing evidence**.
Cite the document and section for every claim. Never change or run product code while learning.
lessons.try: Pick one starter prompt and write down which document section supports each sentence of the answer.

lessons.title: The Messages layer
lessons.hook: Messages are NOT toasts. They are request/response classes: each decides cache vs server.
goals: Explain what a message class is and how it chooses between cache and server
Tell Messages apart from overlay dialogs and sync workers
points: Each class inherits `BaseMessage`; `MessageTransactions` is the facade Product Details calls.
`DataSource`: **Cache**, **Server**, **CacheOrServer**, **ServerOrCache**; `MODE`: `OFFLINE_RET` / `ONLINE_RET`.
Different from `MessageOverlay` (UI dialogs) and `SyncMessages` (Force Sync workers) – three 'message' families!

quiz.q: CacheOrServer with an EMPTY Mongo and network online does what?
quiz.why: Try Mongo first; if empty, call OData.

prompts: What is the Messages layer and how does it decide between the local cache and the server?

lessons.title: OData & eAtlas code
lessons.hook: Same database, two different stacks.
goals: Compare the OData and eAtlas technology stacks
Explain why both use the same shared SQL database
points: **OData**: ASP.NET Web API 2 on IIS, .NET Framework 4.8.1, route `/odata` (v3, batch), contexts: `AlmanacContext`, `LicensingContext`, `MTPContext`.
**eAtlas**: ASP.NET Core 3.1, EF Core `AlmanacContext`, controllers + `Repository/`, SignalR hubs, React/Vite in `clientappvite/`.

quiz.q: Which ORM does eAtlas use?
quiz.why: eAtlas AlmanacContext uses EF Core; OData uses EF6.
